title: SmallRatio: Dedekind sums along Euclid's algorithm and the small-ratio formula
abstract: For a prime p and 0 < h < p, the Dedekind sum s(h,p) is determined, up to an explicit error of order log p, by the fractions of small height congruent to plus or minus h: with the sum over the coprime pairs u, v >= 1 with uv < p/2, |12 s(h,p) - p sum ([hv = u mod p] - [hv = -u mod p])/(uv)| <= 6n <= 12 log_2 p + 6, where n is the length of Euclid's algorithm on (p, h). Summed over any set H of residues, in particular over a subgroup of odd order, this gives |12 sum_{h in H} s(h,p) - p S_H(p)| <= |H| (12 log_2 p + 6), where S_H(p) is the signed sum of 1/(uv) over the coprime pairs with uv < p/2 and u/v in H or -H. The development proves Dedekind reciprocity from scratch (by counting lattice points), the identities of Euclid's algorithm and the bound n <= 2 log_2 k + 1, the alternating-sum form 12 s(h,k) = sum (-1)^{j+1} k/(r_j q_{j-1}) + E with |E| <= 4n, and Legendre's pairing of the small coprime pairs with the steps of the algorithm, by a lattice-basis argument instead of continued fractions.
